1  J UD GME N T
The present petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under; The petitioner is the legally wedded wife of respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 27.08.2010.
They have a girl child by name Poorvi N born on 14.04.2014.

After the marriage the petitioner and respondent started to live at matrimonial house situated at Kempegowdanagara, Gooleharavi with her in laws and they led happy marital life only for few months after that respondent and his family members ill treated the petitioner and started to demand dowry from her parents.

Further respondent made the petitioner to go to her parents house situated at Bangalore thereafter also the  3  Crl.Misc.129/2019 respondent personally as well as telepathically tortured her and her parents and demanded dowry for a sum of Rs.20 lakhs.

When she and her parents were unable to fulfill the demands of the respondent and his family members they started to ill treat by abusing, assaulting and torturing physically and causing mental agony to the petitioner.
Further respondent and his family members threatened to do away with the life of the petitioner and her family members.
The respondent has not provided food and clothing and shelter for her livelihood.

Petitioner further submits that she tolerated the atrocities of the respondent under the impression that one or the other day respondent will improve and realize his mistakes and will take the petitioner to the matrimonial home and they may live happily.

Further she submits that, respondent never came to look after the pregnant woman before giving birth to a child and further not even a single day the respondent or his parents came to see the child as well as the petitioner.
Further she submits that, she went to the respondent's house many times and petitioner was pushed out of the matrimonial house without any valid reasons.
Further she submits that, respondent and his family members picked up a quarrel near the house of the petitioner and forcibly sent the petitioner to her father house.

Further  4  Crl.Misc.129/2019 Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
2 she submits that, she is not having any avocation of her own and she is a home maker and her father's income is very low and they are unable to take care of the petitioner.

entities.text: Crl.Misc.129/2019 Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further she submits that, respondent is an employee in Government Department as a First Division Clerk in BEO Office at Tumkur and he getting a monthly salary of Rs.65,000/- and he is getting monthly income around one lakh from agriculture property and other sources.
In spite of having sufficient source of income he neglected to maintain her and her child.
Hence, this petition.

3. After the service of notice, respondent appeared before this court through his counsel and filed statement of objection and in the statement of objection he has admitted his relationship with the petitioner and admitted that they have daughter from the wedlock and he denied all the other allegations.
He has stated that, he and his family members never demanded dowry and they never caused domestic violence against the petitioner.
Further he submits that, he admitted his daughter to school and he has borne the entire educational expenses of the child.

Further he submits that, he is residing at Tumkur as he is working at BEO Office, Tumkur and he owns ancestral property near Tumkur and he is not  5  Crl.Misc.129/2019 intending to reside at Bengaluru
but the petitioner forced him to reside in Bengaluru and to arrange a house at Bengaluru and when he denied petitioner's demand she voluntarily deserted him and went to her parents house.

Further after a panchayath was convened for reunion, he rented a house at Tumkur and admitted his daughter to a school at Tumkur but there also petitioner and her parents picked up a quarrel with him and again petitioner went to her parents house.
Further he submits that, petitioner restricted her daughter to talk with him.
Further he submits that he is not receiving salary of Rs.65,000/-.
Further he submits that, after deducting loan he is receiving salary of Rs.26,000/- per month.
Further he submits that, till now he is paying the rent of the Tumkur house which was arranged by him for the petitioner.
Further he submits that, he has not deserted the petitioner, the petitioner has voluntarily deserted him and started to reside at her parents house.
On all these grounds he prays to dismiss the petition filed by the petitioner.
4. The petitioner to substantiate her case has Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
3 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 4.

The respondent has led his evidence and got marked Ex.R.1 to 11.
 6  Crl.Misc.129/2019  5.
Heard arguments on both sides.

6. The following points that arises for my consideration are as under;
 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that  she was subjected to Domestic  Violence by the respondent?
 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled  for the reliefs as sought in the  petition?
 3. What order?
The  7  Crl.Misc.129/2019 respondent has neglected the petitioner and her child without any reasonable cause and the respondent is capable to provide maintenance to the petitioner.
9. In this case, there is no dispute regarding the relationship between parties.
Hence, it is proved that the petitioner and the respondent are in a domestic relationship.

It is also an admitted fact that, the Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
4 petitioner and respondent resided together till the date of separation.
Hence they have resided together in a shared household.
It is also not disputed they have one child i.e., Kum.Poorvi N.
The child also resided with the petitioner and respondent.
Hence, petitioner and her child are in a domestic relationship with the respondent in a shared household.
Only the aspect of domestic violence needs to be proved by the petitioner.

10. In order to prove that, the respondents have committed domestic violence, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and filed her affidavit in lieu of examination in chief wherein she has reiterated the contents of her petition.
The petitioner has submitted that, the respondent and his family have demanded dowry of Rs.20 lakhs and also household articles and apartment or site in Bengaluru.
When her parents were  8  Crl.Misc.129/2019 not able to fulfill the demands of the respondent he has started ill treating her, abusing her, assaulting and torturing her.
Hence, she was forced to leave to her parents house.
She has alleged that, the respondent never looked after her even when she was pregnant and he and his parents never came to see the child or her.
She has stated that, she has taken a rented house for herself and she requires money for advance and to pay the rent of the house.
In this regard she has produced rent agreement dated 05.07.2019 which discloses that she has paid Rs.80,000/- as advance and Rs.8,000/- per monthly rent to the house owner.
She has stated that,
her parents
have arranged for the said amount

. She has further stated that, she requires Rs.12,000/- for domestic expenses and her child's expenses, Rs.10,000/-
for other expenses and monthly maintenance of Rs.20,000/-.
She has stated that since the respondent is a government employee and getting monthly income of Rs.;65,000/- he is capable of maintaining her.
11. The respondent in this case has contended that the petitioner was not willing to residing with him in Tumkur and she wished to reside in Bengaluru.

Hence,
she has voluntarily left the matrimonial home.
In this background it is necessary to consider the Cross  9  Crl.Misc.129/2019 Examination of the petitioner.

In her Cross Examination Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
5

entities.text: Cross Examination Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: she has stated that she was not aware about the divorce petition filed by the respondent against her.
Thereafter, when she got to know about the said petition she has appeared before the concerned Court.
She has submitted that, she has resided with the respondent for 8 years, out of which she resided with him at Shira for one year and in Tumkur for rest of the period.
She has admitted that, her mother in law was residing in respondent's native village at that time.

She has admitted that, the respondent's native village is 3 k.m.
away from Tumkur and it is possible for children to go to school at Tumkur from the said village and there are school buses available.
She has stated that, the respondent rented at house at Tumkur after a panchayath was conducted between them.

She has denied all the other suggestions put forth to her and stated that, she resided in a separate house only after it was resolved in the panchayath that herself and respondent should stay in the separate house.
She has admitted that she has not given any complaint to the police against the respondent and she does not have any documents to show that the respondent has assaulted her.
She has stated that she has left the matrimonial home in July 2019.
12. The respondent has admitted that he has filed for divorce against the petitioner in MC 256/2019 and he has produced the copy of the order sheet as Ex.R.1.
He has stated that, the petitioner did not appear before the Hon'ble Family Court and she was placed ex-parte.
Thereafter the said Hon'ble Court granted him divorce by its judgment dated 17.01.2020.
The said Judgment is produced by the respondent and it is marked as Ex.R.4.
On perusal of the judgment it is seen that the said divorce petition was filed on 20.09.2019 and the address of the respondent i.e., the petitioner herein is stated as Manchalakuppe, Tumkur.
It is the case of the respondent that the petitioner's family members are all residing in Bengaluru and even her parents are residing at Bengaluru.
Therefore, petitioner wanted to reside in Bengaluru.
It is also his case that, the petitioner is residing with her parents.
In this background it is pertinent to note that he has given Manchalakuppe address in the divorce case.
In this regard in his Cross Examination respondent has stated that he has given her permanent address.

As per the case of both petitioner and respondent the petitioner left the matrimonial home in July 2019 and the respondent has filed for divorce in September 2019 that too by giving her Manchalakuppe address knowing well that the petitioner Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
6  11  Crl.Misc.129/2019 is not residing in the said address.
Thereafter, he has obtained ex-parte divorce in MC No.256/2019 by Judgment dated 17.01.2020.
Subsequently the respondent even remarried.
He has a 9 month old baby from the remarriage.
Further present petition was filed by the petitioner on 08.07.2019 and petitioner has given her Yelahanka New Town address along with her Manchalakuppe address in the present petition.
The respondent has been duly served in the present petition and he has appeared through his counsel on 06.09.2019.
The divorce petition in MC No.256/2019 was filed on 20.09.2019 I.e, after this petition was filed.

Therefore,
the respondent was very well aware about the Bengaluru address of the petitioner.
But he has given her Manchalakuppe address in divorce proceedings.
All through the present proceedings the respondent has appeared before this Court and this matter was even referred to mediation before the Hon'ble Family Court.
Burt he has not informed the petitioner about MC 256/2019 and he has obtained an exparte order against the petitioner on 17.01.2020.
This in itself shows that the respondent was not interested in continuing matrimonial life with the petitioner.
He has stealthily obtained an exparte divorce decree against the petitioner.
Admittedly, the respondent has not given any notice for  12  Crl.Misc.129/2019 restitution of conjugal rights or even tried to convene a panchayath with family members till date.
He has also not filed for custody or visitation rights of the child till date.
This conduct of the respondent proves that he was least interested in continuing his marital life with the petitioner.
The conduct of the respondent itself constitutes domestic violence.
13. The respondent has contended that, he has paid for the school fees and other expenses of the child.
However he has not produced any documents to prove his contention.

He has submitted that the Hon'ble Family Court in MC 256/2019 by its order dated 21.10.2022 has ordered for interim maintenance of Rs.6,000/- per month to the petitioner from the date of the application till disposal of the petition and has also ordered litigation expenses of Rs.5,000/- to the petitioner.

In Cross Examination respondent has submitted that, he is paying the said interim Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
7 maintenance regularly.
But before the said order for interim maintenance the respondent has not paid any amount to the petitioner or her child.
This also proves the economic abuse caused by the respondent.

Further the respondent has contended that, petitioners siblings are all government employees and earning Rs.65,000/-
 13  Crl.Misc.129/2019 per month.
Even her father is a retired government employee and has many immovable properties in Tumkur and Bengaluru.
Therefore, the petitioner does not required any maintenance.

But it is settled law by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manish Jain V/s Akanksha Jain reported in AIR 2017 Supreme Court 1640, that the income of the parents should not be considered while deciding the maintenance of the parties.

entities.text: Manish Jain V/s Akanksha Jain reported in AIR 2017 Supreme Court 1640
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the salary of the siblings of the petitioner and properties of the father of the petitioner is immaterial for the present case.
14. In the present case respondent has admittedly not paid any maintenance to the petitioner and her child from the date of separation.
As already stated this constitutes economic abuse as contemplated in PWDV Act.
Therefore, it is proved that the respondent has committed domestic violence against the petitioner.
Hence, point No.1 answered in the affirmative.
15. POINT No.2 :-
The petitioner in this case has sought for Rs.20,000/- monthly maintenance.
Admittedly, the petitioner is unemployed.
She has studied up to SSLC.
She has stated that, she requires Rs.40,000/- for her monthly maintenance.

Minor child  14  Crl.Misc.129/2019 aged 8 years who is studying in Sheshadripuram School,
Yelahanka is in her care and custody.
Petitioner has stated that she requires Rs.1.5 lakhs towards child maintenance and education.
Petitioner has stated that she is residing with her parents.
She has stated that she is incurring litigation expenses of Rs.5,000/-.
The Hon'ble Family Court in MC No.256/2019 has ordered interim maintenance of Rs.6,000/- per month to the petitioner and litigation expenses of Rs.5,000/-.

16. On the other hand the respondent is working Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
8 as a Superintendent in BEO office, Nelamangala and he is earning Rs.52,881/- per month as per his assets and liabilities affidavit.
He has stated that, he has monthly expenditure of Rs.54,128/-.
He has stated that, he has remarried and he has his 2nd wife, 9 months old baby from the said marriage.
He has stated that, his aged mother and his 2nd wife and child are his dependents.
He has stated that he has paid Rs.30,000/- per annum towards education of the petitioner's child.
However, he has not substantiated this expenditure with documents.
The petitioner has not admitted regarding this payment made by the respondent.
Therefore, the respondent has to prove that he has paid Rs.30,000/- per annum towards his child education.
But the respondent has not  15  Crl.Misc.129/2019 proved this aspect.
He has stated that, he has availed loan of Rs.17,228/-.
He has stated that, he has availed a personal loan.
He has stated that, he is paying rent of Rs.6,000/- for his house.
17 . It is proved by discussion in point No.1 that the respondent has committed domestic violence against the petitioner and her child.
The respondent has paid interim maintenance only after Hon'ble Family Court has passed orders.

There is no straight jacket formula to award maintenance and it is settled principle of law that the status of parties, their earning capacity, their expenses, their dependents, the prevailing market conditions etc have to be taken into consideration while awarding maintenance.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324, the Court has to consider the status of the parties, earning capacity of the parties,
needs and expenses of the petitioner, number of dependents on the respondent, expenses of the respondent, educational qualification of the parties,
whether the petitioner has independent source and whether the same is sufficient to enable her to maintain herself, standard of living as she was accustomed to in the matrimonial home, whether she was working before  16  Crl.Misc.129/2019 marriage, cost of litigation for a non working wife etc.,
while ordering for maintenance.

entities.text: Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying these propositions of law, the respondent is directed to pay maintenance of Rs.10,000/- per month towards the maintenance of petitioner and Rs.10,000/- towards Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/
9 minor child.

18. The petitioner has sought for protection order directing the respondent not to interfere with the peaceful life of the petitioner, she has also sought for an order of safety by imposing certain conditions against the respondent from causing any harm to the petitioner and she has also sought for an order directing the Yelahanka police to give protection to the petitioner from the respondent.
As already stated the petitioner and respondent are not residing together.
Petitioner has not proved that the respondent has interfered in her life or has threatened her or her minor child's safety after separation.
Hence, it is not necessary to pass protection order against the respondent.
Hence,point No.2 answered partly in the affirmative.

19. POINT No.3 :- In view of the materials placed before this court, pleadings, deposition and documentary evidence this court proceed to pass the following;
 17  Crl.Misc.129/2019  ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 as against respondent is allowed in part.

Further, respondent is hereby directed to pay an amount of Rs.10,000/-per month (Rupees ten thousand only) to the petitioner's minor child by name Poorvi towards maintenance from the date of petition till her marriage.
Crl.Misc.129/2019
Amount if any already paid by the respondent towards monthly maintenance of the petitioner till today is set off from the above said monthly maintenance amount awarded to her.
